headline: SITCON 4 (GUARDED): OpenSSH 'SSHole' exploitation continues; Iris Plaza breach may expose 7.7M; GitHub secret abuse persists

bullets.text: New since the 15:20 SITREP: 6 new reports (2 high, 3 medium, 1 low); SITCON holds at 4 (GUARDED). Both high items extend running stories: SecurityWeek reports hackers exploiting the 'SSHole' OpenSSH auth bypass, and Iris Plaza's breach. The last 7 days scored 0.82x the 90-day average.

OpenSSH: CVE-2026-123158 ('SSHole') was exploited in the wild hours after disclosure. OpenSSH issued an emergency fix for the flaw, which lets long passwords bypass SSH auth on Alpine Linux and also reaches routers.
Iris Plaza / Iris Ohyama: a cloud breach at the Japanese homeware company may have exposed 7.7 million customer records, and it has pulled its online store.

GitHub secrets: hackers are using Artex to scan GitHub repositories for exposed secrets; Microsoft reports threat actors using agentic AI tooling to find and abuse them; Truffle Security is revoking nearly 1.5 million live secrets.
Network gear: Zyxel GS1900 switches were hacked through a zero-day (CVE-2026-107441) that an earlier patch failed to block; D-Link warned of multiple zero-days in DGS-3130 Series switches.

Other breaches this week: Amplifon Americas (1.3 million people), Frontline Education (3M+), Chainalysis (credentials for all customers exposed) and a $133 million French bank heist via a service provider.

actions: Clear KEV items due tomorrow: Adobe Commerce/Magento CVE-2026-48356 and Brotli CVE-2026-111497 (11-10), then VMware ESX CVE-2026-41709 (11-11).
Patch OpenSSH on every internet-facing host for CVE-2026-123158, prioritising Alpine Linux and routers; restrict SSH exposure and review auth logs.
Scan GitHub repos and their history for committed secrets; revoke and rotate anything found and enable secret scanning with push protection.
Zyxel GS1900 and D-Link DGS-3130 owners: apply the vendors' latest fixes or mitigations and check switches for signs of compromise.
Patch Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-104935 (KEV due 11-13) and SonicWall SSL-VPN CVE-2026-19868 (due 11-20); review VPN logs for logins that skipped MFA.
Iris Ohyama, Amplifon, Frontline Education and Chainalysis customers: reset passwords, rotate API keys and credentials, and watch for phishing.
